summary: Round r1 (restricted network; data hosts blocked; no WebSearch used - all leads reused from 27B/27C plus three multilateral transit-law texts marked 'URL from general knowledge - unverified'). Q1 (is each hypothetical arrangement incentive-compatible and enforceable?) is answered with conditional statuses, never probabilities. 27B arrangements: HA-1 long-term PPA FEASIBLE_IF nine conditions (price band, national-value W_NN >= 0, regime restriction, damages, approval-tenor, capacity, eligibility, ratification, outside-option drift); HA-2 energy banking FEASIBLE_IF (return-leg security is binding); HA-3 trilateral sale FEASIBLE_IF (approval state exogenous; payment security and Bangladesh-side approval missing from 27B); HA-4 joint interconnector UNDETERMINED (India-side benefit unspecified; discount rate unregistered); HA-5 transit service UNDETERMINED (fee choice set may be fixed by treaty and multilateral transit law). 27C structures: SO-01, SO-02, SO-04, SO-05, SO-07, SO-08, SO-09 FEASIBLE_IF; SO-03, SO-06, SO-10 UNDETERMINED; 27D crisis sequencing UNDETERMINED pending its eligibility matrix. No arrangement is marked INFEASIBLE because no retrieved evidence supports it; infeasibility triggers are listed. Welfare conflicts are mapped to the 12 objectives as channels with unknown direction. All empirical items pending; no numbers recorded. Nothing here represents any government's position or intentions.

Method: national feasibility (22E opportunity cost, domestic transfers netted) and entity feasibility (seller/utility payoffs including C_PPA_t) are evaluated separately; an arrangement is reported FEASIBLE only where both hold or the divergence is stated.

Opportunity costs follow 22E regimes (spill / export-marginal / import-marginal) and 27B-A2.

challenges.text: HA-1 conditions are incomplete: (i) add a national-value participation condition W_NN >= 0 alongside seller participation - with C_PPA_t below p_c the seller can gain while the nation loses in import-marginal blocks; (ii) restrict firm delivery to spill/export-marginal regimes or price the import-marginal OC_t explicitly; (iii) specify dispute forum/governing law so d_S and d_B are enforceable; (iv) add outside-option drift over the tenor (S09/S04 price paths) and an indexation/reopener term as a decision variable.

HA-2 asserts that the return obligation falls in the counterparty's high-price season; this is an unverified empirical premise - mark it pending on 22B block-level prices by Nepali month. Also add a sequencing (first-mover) IC evaluated at the dry-leg date and the regulatory treatment of banked energy.

HA-3 omits the buyer-side procurement/regulatory approval, contract currency, convertibility and payment-security terms; the payoff uses a generic FX without payment-delay risk. Add these as conditions.

HA-4 cannot be audited on the India side: B_I 'system benefits' are unattributed, so IC4-individual is undefined. Also CRF needs a discount rate and asset life that are not in the parameter register - register them as labelled assumptions (config/model_config.yaml owners) with bounds. Add safeguard/right-of-way constraints.

HA-5 treats f_r as freely negotiable; fees and procedures may be fixed by the transit treaty/protocol and bounded by multilateral transit law (GATT Art. V, TFA Art. 11 - to verify). Also e_r is defined as an 'expected' cost, which implies a diversion probability; restate as documented procedure cost. The value of time h has no source or assumption label.
No HA is mapped to the 12 welfare objectives or to scenarios; 27E has added channels and scenario links - please adopt or contest them in r2.

Structure options list feasibility conditions but no counterparty payoff or enforcement mechanism; SO-03 and SO-06 are UNDETERMINED for that reason. Please specify the anchor investor/buyer outside option and the enforcement instrument (guarantee, treaty, contract forum) for each option.
27D-COORD cannot be audited until the eligibility matrix, concurrent-facility sequencing rules and documentary prerequisites promised in outputs_to_27E are delivered.

No contract layer exists in energy.MarginalUseComparison (27B's challenge); 27E feasibility statuses cannot be computed in code until p_c band, damages and approval state are implemented. Also add catalog ids for WTO legal texts and UN treaty texts if absent.

uncertainty: Very high. Every condition is pending, so no status can move from conditional to settled in r1. Structural uncertainty: unilateral approval regimes may dominate price terms; entity and national feasibility can diverge; comparator evidence may not transfer; legal texts may fix variables that 27B treats as negotiable. Statuses are conditional classifications, not forecasts or probabilities, and say nothing about any government's intentions.

feasibility_findings.question: Q1 Is each hypothetical arrangement incentive-compatible and enforceable?
feasibility_findings.answer_status: Answered as conditional statuses only. Every arrangement is either FEASIBLE_IF (exact conditions and the pending evidence that settles each) or UNDETERMINED (why, and what would convert it). No arrangement is marked INFEASIBLE: no retrieved evidence supports that; infeasibility triggers are listed per arrangement. No probabilities are assigned.

status_taxonomy.FEASIBLE_IF: a contract/structure satisfying all parties' participation and enforceability conditions exists if every listed condition holds; each condition maps to pending evidence
status_taxonomy.INFEASIBLE_IF: listed triggers under which no admissible contract exists; used as a status only when evidence shows a trigger holds
status_taxonomy.UNDETERMINED: the condition set cannot be written or evaluated (missing payoff, undefined choice set or unresolved documented conflict)

feasibility_findings.method: For each arrangement: (1) incentive compatibility = participation of every modelled party against its documented outside option, no-deviation (diversion/walkaway) conditions, and physical/legal feasibility (capacity, eligibility, approval, ratification); national value (22E OC_t) checked separately from entity-level payoffs; (2) enforceability = who can compel performance, in which forum, and which obligations sit outside any contract (unilateral approvals); (3) opportunity costs from 22E and fiscal owners; (4) conflicts with the 12 objectives in src/economic_model/welfare.py recorded as channels with direction '?' until evidenced; (5) scenario links for stress tests.

arrangements.name: Hypothetical long-term power-purchase arrangement (seller in Nepal, buyer in India)
arrangements.status_basis: Structure admits a feasible contract under stated conditions; no condition can yet be evaluated because every parameter is pending. Status is conditional, not a probability or a forecast.

conditions: F1 price band non-empty: q-weighted (P_ALT_t - C_TX_IN - C_TRD) >= q-weighted (OC_t + C_TX_NP)/FX_INR over the months/blocks actually contracted (27B IC1-feasible-price-band).

F2 national-value condition (added by 27E): W_NN >= 0 in addition to U_NS >= outside option; a contract can satisfy seller participation (C_PPA_t below p_c) while the national payoff is negative when contracted blocks fall in the import-marginal regime (OC_t = P_IMP_t + delivery cost). Both must hold.

F3 regime restriction (added by 27E): contracted q_t is confined to spill or export-marginal regimes, or p_c clears the import-marginal OC_t in any block where a firm delivery obligation falls in the dry season.
F4 damages: d_S and d_B satisfy 27B IC1-no-diversion-NS and IC1-no-walkaway-IB on block-level price distributions, and the damages are enforceable in a named forum (see enforceability).
F5 approval-tenor: either V_A >= T, or renewal criteria are text-specified, or both parties' participation holds in the state A_t = 0 from the first renewal date (27B IC1-approval-tenor).
F6 capacity: sum q_t per block <= min(Cap_X, approved quantum) net of committed flows.
F7 eligibility: allocated generating assets meet the 2018 Guidelines eligibility clauses as amended (04C CM-01).
F8 ratification: if the arrangement falls in the constitutional natural-resource category, parliamentary ratification is completed (route pending from Supreme Court verdict text).

F9 outside-option drift (added by 27E): participation re-checked under the scenario price paths of S09 (regional electricity-market transformation) and S04, not only on historical block prices; otherwise p_c needs an indexation or reopener clause, whose terms are then a decision variable.
evidence_to_settle: 22B/22E block-level P_IEX, P_EXP, C_TRD, C_TX_IN, C_TX_NP, P_IMP by Nepali month
22E regime classification per month/block (needs 05A spill/limit data)
V_A and renewal criteria from CEA DA procedure and approval orders
Supreme Court verdict text on ratification route
S09/S04 price-path assumptions from scenario owners

issues: Approval layer (IR) is unilateral and outside the contract: no private remedy can compel A_t = 1, so enforceability of volume commitments rests on the approval-lapse clause and on any government-to-government linkage clause in the 2014 agreement (to verify).

Dispute forum and governing law for cross-border damages are not specified in 27B; enforcement of an award against a state-owned counterparty depends on documented dispute clauses (to locate in the 2014 agreement and any 2024 long-term agreement text).
Deviation-settlement charges under CBTE act as a regulatory floor on non-delivery cost; interaction with contractual d_S pending.
Repeated-game support: in a long tenor, continuation value can sustain compliance, but no reputation parameter is estimated or attributed to any party.

opportunity_costs: Nepal national: OC_t by 22E regime; zero only in spill blocks.
Domestic-industry alternative DNV_t (22E) for MWh locked in over the tenor - long tenor forecloses later domestic use if DNV_t rises above ENV_t.
Seller: best of spot export (ENV_spot_t) and domestic sale.
Fiscal: take-or-pay or delivery damages borne by a state utility are contingent liabilities (26A/02 to record).
infeasible_if: F1 fails in every contracted season (band empty).
F7 fails for all assets proposed for allocation.
Approved quantum is zero for the relevant route and no approval process is available.

arrangements.name: Hypothetical seasonal energy-banking (wet-season delivery against dry-season return)
arrangements.status_basis: Conditional on the beta band being non-empty and the return leg being enforceable; the enforceability condition is the binding design issue. Not a probability.

conditions: G1 beta band non-empty: 27B IC2-NS floor <= IC2-IB ceiling on q-weighted block values.

G2 sequencing (added by 27E): because Nepal delivers first, the counterparty's incentive to return in the dry leg must hold at the dry-leg date, not ex ante: U_IB evaluated from the dry-leg start must be non-negative, else a cash-settlement fallback at a stated index or collateral is required.
G3 approvals: export-leg and import-leg approvals are separate instruments; both must be valid for their seasons (A_t for both legs).
G4 capacity for each leg per block.

G5 seasonality premise (challenge to 27B): 27B states that the return obligation falls in the counterparty's high-price season; this is an empirical premise that must be verified from 22B block-level Indian price data by Nepali month before it is used.
evidence_to_settle: 22B block-level Indian prices by Nepali month (wet and dry legs)
import approval orders with hours and validity (27B-L33 locator; primary order required)
CBTE treatment of banked energy and deviation settlement

issues: Non-simultaneous exchange creates a one-sided exposure for the first mover; enforceable only with a security instrument (cash-settlement index, escrow or letter of credit) whose availability under exchange-control rules is pending (27B-L23).
Accounting treatment of banked energy under Indian cross-border regulations is not documented in 27B; if banking is not recognised, the arrangement must be restated as two cash trades.

opportunity_costs: Wet leg: OC_w (zero in spill blocks, ENV_t otherwise).
Dry leg: avoided P_IMP_d; foregone alternative dry-season supply routes.
Fiscal: security instrument cost.
infeasible_if: G1 fails (floor above ceiling).
Banked energy has no recognised regulatory treatment and no cash-settlement alternative is available.

arrangements.name: Hypothetical shared cross-border transmission (jointly owned interconnector with cost and capacity-rent sharing)
arrangements.status_basis: The India-side participation condition cannot be written: 27B leaves B_I 'system benefits' unattributed, so the core of the cost game (IC4-individual) is not defined on one side. Nepal-side status is FEASIBLE_IF (below). Becomes FEASIBLE_IF for both sides once B_I is specified from documented planning criteria, or once a regulated-tariff route makes R_X cover K_X*CRF + OM_X (in which case sharing reduces to ownership shares).

conditions: J1 aggregate: B_N + B_I + R_X >= K_X*CRF + OM_X.

J2 Nepal-side (FEASIBLE_IF): IC4-individual holds for NX with B_N evaluated at currently approved quanta only (hold-up robust), or a clause links trade approval to line capacity (to find in 2014 agreement / JV texts).

J3 discount rate (challenge to 27B): CRF requires a discount rate and asset life; these are unlisted parameters and must be registered as labelled assumptions in config/model_config.yaml, with sensitivity bounds.
J4 regulated vs merchant: the tariff route (ERC and CERC determinations for each segment) decides whether R_X is cost-plus (sharing trivial) or capacity-rent (sharing depends on price spreads).
evidence_to_settle: JV agreements for the October 2025 lines (news locator only)
tariff determination route for cross-border segments on each side
capital cost and O&M from project documents

issues: Joint ownership creates mutual hostage (sunk assets on both sides), which supports compliance, but the benefits B_N depend on unilateral approvals set for shorter periods than line life (hold-up).
Asset split across a border: which jurisdiction's regulator sets tariff for each segment is pending.

opportunity_costs: Capital cost K_X versus domestic transmission investment (05 owners).
Public equity and debt service versus other public investment (fiscal_financial).
infeasible_if: J1 fails.

arrangements.name: Hypothetical transit-service arrangement (third-country cargo through a transit state to a port)
arrangements.status_basis: 27B treats the transit fee f_r as a negotiable variable, but fees and procedures may be fixed or bounded by existing treaty/protocol texts and by multilateral transit law; until those texts are read the choice set itself is unknown. Also e_r is labelled 'expected enforcement cost', which implies a probability of diversion; it must be restated as documented procedure costs. Becomes FEASIBLE_IF once the legally admissible range of f_r and procedures is established.

conditions: K1 admissible fee range from transit treaty/protocol and, where applicable, GATT Article V / TFA Article 11 (to verify applicability and text).
K2 IC5-joint on the admissible range: c_ref - c_r - tau_r*h >= a_r + e_r - m_r.
K3 value of time h: an unlisted parameter requiring a documented source (e.g. inventory-carrying cost method) or a labelled assumption with bounds.
K4 northern-route comparison (04C CM-04): c_ref must be defined per origin/destination; a single reference route mixes distinct markets.
evidence_to_settle: Treaty of Transit and protocol text; Nepal-China transit protocol text
route costs and dwell times from dry-port/project documents
WTO membership and applicability for the transit states concerned

issues: Transit is governed by government-to-government instruments with periodic renewal; renewal and review clauses determine credibility.
Customs guarantee/sealing procedures trade off diversion control against cost and time (the e_r vs c_r, tau_r trade-off).

opportunity_costs: Existing route costs; investment in alternative corridors (S02).
infeasible_if: No fee within the admissible range satisfies K2 for any route (route unused).

cross_cutting_findings: The unilateral approval state A_t is the dominant enforceability constraint for HA-1..HA-4 and SO-01/SO-02: it cannot be secured by any private contract, so every electricity arrangement is at best FEASIBLE_IF evaluated in both approval states.
Entity-level feasibility (seller participation) and national feasibility (W_NN >= 0) can diverge; both must be reported.
No arrangement is assessed as GDP-positive; GDP effects enter only via sector value added, and every conflict channel remains '?' until observations exist.
feasibility_findings.hypothetical_label: All arrangements are hypothetical research constructs by NEPAL 3T. This audit does not state, predict or represent the positions, preferences, bargaining power or intentions of any government, utility or institution.
